summary: Aegis Health Console is an astronaut health monitoring platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.. The platform features a centralised dashboard for recording vital indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep, and mood. It uses a colour-coded green, amber, and red assessment system to identify potential health concerns and suggest appropriate actions. A key feature is its interactive 3D human body visualisation, featuring male and female anatomical models. The body explorer connects different organs and body systems with spaceflight-related risks such as radiation, altered gravity, isolation, and confinement. The platform also incorporates the ZOE interactive health-scanning experience. Additional features include historical health tracking, visual analytics, daily wellness routines, mental health monitoring, and a Flight Surgeon Console for medical supervision. Built using React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, the application follows an offline-first architecture with local data storage and optional cloud synchronisation through a Node.js and SQLite backend.
details: Aegis Health Console is a health monitoring software project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It is designed to help astronauts monitor and manage their physical and mental well-being during long-duration space missions, where communication with Earth may be delayed or limited. The platform provides a centralised dashboard to record vital health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep duration, and mood. Its major features include interactive 3D male and female anatomical models, a ZOE health-scanning interface, and a body system explorer that demonstrates how spaceflight hazards such as radiation, altered gravity, isolation, and confinement affect the human body. It also offers colour-coded health assessments, historical health analytics, daily wellness routines, mental health monitoring, and a Flight Surgeon Console for medical supervision. The application is built using React 19, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, with Recharts for data visualisation and Motion for animations. Its optional backend uses Node.js, Hono, and SQLite. The offline-first architecture allows astronauts to access and record health information without continuous internet connectivity, synchronising data when communication becomes available. The project's overall goal is to empower astronauts with accessible health information and decision-support tools, enabling them to recognise potential abnormalities and make informed health decisions independently.
